1926-01-01.head: Turkey Adopts International Calendar and Time
1926-01-01.body: Turkey has from today abandoned the traditional reckoning of dates and hours and adopted the international calendar and clock.

1926-01-01.head: Rhine Floods Drive 50,000 From Cologne
1926-01-01.body: The Rhine has burst upon Cologne, rising 35 feet in the worst flood there for more than a century. Some 50,000 residents have been forced from their homes.

1926-01-01.head: Irish Free State Opens Broadcasting Service
1926-01-01.body: Dr Douglas Hyde has formally opened 2RN, the first broadcasting station of the Irish Free State, which began regular programmes in Dublin today.

1926-01-02.head: Floods Ravage Europe From England to Romania
1926-01-02.body: Heavy rains and unseasonably warm weather have brought floods across the Continent, from England to Romania.

1926-01-02.head: British Contributory Old Age Pensions Begin
1926-01-02.body: Contributory old age pensions became payable in Great Britain today to insured persons between 65 and 70 years of age.

1926-01-02.head: Death of Physiologist Richard Caton
1926-01-02.body: Dr Richard Caton, the Liverpool physiologist who in 1875 demonstrated the electrical currents of the brain, has died aged 83.

1926-01-03.head: Pangalos Assumes Dictatorial Powers in Greece
1926-01-03.body: General Theodoros Pangalos, Prime Minister of Greece since June's coup, has declared a state of emergency and assumed dictatorial powers.

1926-01-04.head: Queen Mother Margherita of Italy Dead
1926-01-04.body: Queen Margherita of Savoy, widow of King Umberto I and Queen of Italy from 1878 to 1900, has died aged 74.

1926-01-04.head: Romania Accepts Prince Carol's Renunciation
1926-01-04.body: The Romanian Parliament has accepted Crown Prince Carol's renunciation of his right to the throne. His four-year-old son Michael becomes Crown Prince.

1926-01-04.head: First Widows' Pensions Paid in Britain
1926-01-04.body: Widows' pensions under the new Contributory Pensions Act were paid out at British post offices for the first time today.

1926-01-05.head: Continental Floods Show No Sign of Abating
1926-01-05.body: Rivers across Europe remain in flood after weeks of heavy rain and mild weather, with low-lying districts from England to Romania under water.
1926-01-05.note: No event dated 5 Jan on source page; ongoing European flood story reported 2-7 Jan.

1926-01-06.head: German Airlines Merge Into Luft Hansa
1926-01-06.body: Deutsche Luft Hansa has been formed in Berlin by the merger of Germany's two largest air carriers, Deutscher Aero Lloyd and Junkers Luftverkehr.

1926-01-07.head: Floods Submerge War Graves and London Tubes
1926-01-07.body: Continuing downpours have submerged Great War cemeteries in France and flooded parts of the London Underground railway.

1926-01-07.head: Mussolini Government Creates Royal Academy of Italy
1926-01-07.body: The Fascist government has created a Royal Academy of Italy to promote and coordinate Italian intellectual activity and preserve the national spirit.

1926-01-07.head: Mackenzie King Retains Office as Parliament Meets
1926-01-07.body: Canada's new Parliament has assembled. Mr Mackenzie King continues as Prime Minister with Progressive support, although the Conservatives won more seats and he lost his own.

1926-01-08.head: Ibn Saud Proclaimed King of the Hejaz
1926-01-08.body: At the Grand Mosque of Mecca, Abdul Aziz ibn Saud, Sultan of Nejd, has been proclaimed King of the Hejaz and received the oath of allegiance.

1926-01-08.head: Boy Emperor Bao Dai Crowned at Hue
1926-01-08.body: Prince Vinh Thuy, aged 12, has been crowned Emperor of Annam at the Imperial City of Hue, taking the reign name Bao Dai.

1926-01-09.head: Mexican Rebels Loot and Burn Train
1926-01-09.body: A band of 20 Mexican rebels under Colonel Manuel Nunez opened fire aboard a Guadalajara to Mexico City train, then looted and burned the cars.

1926-01-09.head: American Navy Unready for War, League Says
1926-01-09.body: The Navy League of the United States reports the American fleet unprepared for war and well short of the tonnage permitted under the Washington Treaty.

1926-01-09.head: Tshekedi Khama Named Bamangwato Regent
1926-01-09.body: In the Bechuanaland Protectorate, Tshekedi Khama has been named regent of the Bamangwato for his four-year-old nephew Seretse.

1926-01-10.head: Hernando Siles Sworn In as Bolivian President
1926-01-10.body: Dr Hernando Siles has taken office as President of Bolivia.

1926-01-10.head: Liechtenstein Votes in Landtag Elections
1926-01-10.body: Liechtenstein has held the first round of elections to its 15-member Landtag.

1926-01-10.head: Schooner Capsizes in Miami Harbour
1926-01-10.body: The four-masted Danish schooner Prinz Valdemar has capsized in Biscayne Bay, blocking the harbour channel at Miami.

1926-01-11.head: Congressman Langley Resigns His Seat
1926-01-11.body: United States Representative John W. Langley of Kentucky has resigned from Congress.

1926-01-12.head: Japanese Rayon Company Founded
1926-01-12.body: Toyo Rayon, a new company for the manufacture of artificial silk, has been founded in Japan by the Mitsui interests.

1926-01-13.head: Britain and Iraq Sign New Treaty
1926-01-13.body: A new treaty signed at Baghdad extends the Anglo-Iraqi alliance for 25 years, or until Iraq is admitted to the League of Nations, following the Mosul award.

1926-01-13.head: Oklahoma Mine Explosion Kills 91
1926-01-13.body: An explosion in a coal mine at Wilburton, Oklahoma, has killed 91 miners.

1926-01-14.head: Egyptian Opposition Parties Form Joint Committee
1926-01-14.body: The Wafd, the Liberal Constitutionalists and the National Party have formed an executive committee to concert their response to King Fuad and the Ziwar Pasha ministry.

1926-01-14.head: Total Eclipse Observed in Southern Hemisphere
1926-01-14.body: A total eclipse of the sun was observed across the Indian Ocean. Astronomers gathered in Sumatra to test Einstein's theory of relativity.

1926-01-14.head: French Novelist Rene Boylesve Dies
1926-01-14.body: Rene Boylesve, the French novelist and member of the Academie Francaise, has died aged 58.

1926-01-15.head: Messager Operetta Opens in Paris
1926-01-15.body: Andre Messager's new operetta Passionnement, to a libretto by Albert Willemetz, has opened at the Theatre de la Michodiere in Paris.

1926-01-16.head: Radio Hoax on London Riots Causes Alarm
1926-01-16.body: A British Broadcasting Company play by Father Ronald Knox, describing an imaginary workers' riot in London, caused alarm among listeners who took it for genuine news.

1926-01-17.head: Egyptian Opposition Committee Continues Deliberations
1926-01-17.body: The joint committee of the Wafd, Liberal and Nationalist parties is continuing talks on a common course towards the Ziwar ministry and the question of new elections.
1926-01-17.note: No event dated 17 Jan on source pages; ongoing story from the committee formed 14 Jan.

1926-01-18.head: Negro Voting Rights March in Birmingham
1926-01-18.body: Mrs Indiana Little has led a march of Negro citizens to the courthouse at Birmingham, Alabama, demanding the right to register as voters.

1926-01-19.head: Irish Free State to Mint Own Coinage
1926-01-19.body: Mr Ernest Blythe, Free State Minister for Finance, has introduced a Bill providing for the issue of Irish silver, nickel and bronze coins.

1926-01-20.head: Luther Forms Minority Cabinet in Germany
1926-01-20.body: Chancellor Hans Luther has been obliged to reconstitute his cabinet as a minority government.

1926-01-20.head: Gale Imperils Shipping Off New York
1926-01-20.body: A severe Atlantic gale is threatening several ships off the approaches to New York.

1926-01-21.head: Nobel Laureate Camillo Golgi Dies
1926-01-21.body: Professor Camillo Golgi of Pavia, the Italian histologist who shared the 1906 Nobel Prize for Medicine for his studies of the nervous system, has died aged 82.

1926-01-21.head: Belgian Parliament Ratifies Locarno Treaties
1926-01-21.body: The Belgian Parliament has accepted the Locarno Treaties.

1926-01-22.head: Spanish Flying Boat Sets Out for Buenos Aires
1926-01-22.body: Major Ramon Franco and his crew have left Palos de Moguer in the Dornier flying boat Plus Ultra, attempting to fly from Spain to Buenos Aires.

1926-01-23.head: Cardinal Mercier Dies in Brussels
1926-01-23.body: Cardinal Mercier, Archbishop of Malines, whose defiance of the German occupation made him a national hero of Belgium, has died aged 74.

1926-01-24.head: Cape to Cairo Motor Expedition Arrives
1926-01-24.body: Major Chaplin Court Treatt and his wife Stella have arrived in Cairo from Cape Town, completing the first crossing of Africa by motor car.

1926-01-24.head: Liechtenstein Completes Its Elections
1926-01-24.body: The second round of Liechtenstein's Landtag elections has been held. The Christian-Social People's Party retains its majority.

1926-01-25.head: Surgeon Moynihan Speaks on Cancer
1926-01-25.body: Sir Berkeley Moynihan, the eminent Leeds surgeon, has addressed the public on the prevention of cancer.

1926-01-25.head: Textile Strike Begins at Passaic
1926-01-25.body: Woollen mill workers at Passaic, New Jersey, have walked out in protest against a wage reduction.

1926-01-26.head: Baird Demonstrates Television in London
1926-01-26.body: Mr John Logie Baird has demonstrated his apparatus for transmitting moving images by wireless to members of the Royal Institution and a reporter of The Times.

1926-01-26.head: Plus Ultra Reaches Cape Verde Islands
1926-01-26.body: The Spanish flying boat Plus Ultra has flown 1,081 miles from Las Palmas to Porto Praia in the Cape Verde Islands in under ten hours.

1926-01-27.head: American Senate Votes for World Court
1926-01-27.body: The United States Senate has voted 76 to 17 in favour of adhering to the Permanent Court of International Justice, subject to reservations.

1926-01-28.head: Japanese Premier Viscount Kato Dies
1926-01-28.body: Viscount Kato Takaaki, Prime Minister of Japan, has died of influenza.

1926-01-28.head: Brussels Mourns Cardinal Mercier
1926-01-28.body: Thousands of mourners lined the streets of Brussels for the funeral procession of Cardinal Mercier.

1926-01-28.head: Admiral Sir Ernest Troubridge Dead
1926-01-28.body: Admiral Sir Ernest Troubridge, who commanded the British naval mission in Serbia during the war, has died.

1926-01-29.head: Soviet Law Lifts Limit on Inheritance
1926-01-29.body: A change in Soviet law has effectively removed the limit on the size of estates that may be inherited.

1926-01-29.head: Negro Woman Admitted to Supreme Court Bar
1926-01-29.body: Mrs Violette Anderson of Chicago has become the first Negro woman admitted to practise before the United States Supreme Court.

1926-01-30.head: Wakatsuki Becomes Prime Minister of Japan
1926-01-30.body: Mr Wakatsuki Reijiro, Home Minister, has been appointed Prime Minister of Japan in succession to the late Viscount Kato.

1926-01-30.head: Plus Ultra Crosses the South Atlantic
1926-01-30.body: Major Franco's flying boat has flown 1,429 miles from the Cape Verde Islands to Fernando de Noronha in 12 hours, the longest stage of the flight.

1926-01-30.head: Film Actress Barbara La Marr Dies
1926-01-30.body: Barbara La Marr, the American screen actress, has died in California aged 29.

1926-01-31.head: Allies Evacuate Cologne Zone
1926-01-31.body: British and Belgian troops have left Cologne as the Allied occupation of the first Rhineland zone ends.

1926-01-31.head: Italian Chamber Enlarges Mussolini's Powers
1926-01-31.body: The Italian Chamber has passed Law No. 100, empowering the executive to issue decrees having the force of law.

1926-01-31.head: Plus Ultra Reaches Brazil
1926-01-31.body: Despite engine trouble, the Spanish flying boat Plus Ultra has flown from Fernando de Noronha to Pernambuco, reaching the Brazilian mainland.

1926-02-01.head: Colonel Billy Mitchell Leaves the Army
1926-02-01.body: Colonel William Mitchell, court-martialled advocate of air power, has resigned from the United States Army Air Service.

1926-02-01.head: Record Price for New York Land
1926-02-01.body: Land at the corner of Broadway and Wall Street in New York has been sold at a record $7 a square inch.

1926-02-02.head: Britain and France Sign Palestine-Syria Accord
1926-02-02.body: British and French representatives have signed an agreement of friendship and good neighbourly relations between the mandated territories of Palestine and Syria and the Lebanon.

1926-02-02.head: General Sukhomlinov Dies in Berlin
1926-02-02.body: General Vladimir Sukhomlinov, the Tsar's former Minister of War, has died in poverty in Berlin aged 77.

1926-02-03.head: Pennsylvania Mine Explosion Kills 20
1926-02-03.body: An explosion at a Pittsburgh Terminal Coal Company mine at Horning, Pennsylvania, has killed 20 miners.

1926-02-03.head: Colonel Franco Promoted Brigadier General
1926-02-03.body: Colonel Francisco Franco, commander of the Spanish Foreign Legion in Morocco, has been promoted brigadier general at 33, said to be the youngest general in Europe.

1926-02-04.head: Turkish Cleric Hanged Under Hat Law
1926-02-04.body: Iskilipli Mehmed Atif Hoca, an Islamic scholar who opposed the new hat law, has been hanged in Turkey.

1926-02-04.head: Plus Ultra Arrives at Rio de Janeiro
1926-02-04.body: Major Franco's crew have flown 1,302 miles from Pernambuco to Rio de Janeiro in just over 12 hours.

1926-02-05.head: Soviet Couriers Attacked on Riga Train
1926-02-05.body: Gunmen attacked Soviet diplomatic couriers aboard the Moscow-Riga train in Latvia. Courier Theodor Nette was killed defending the diplomatic bag.

1926-02-06.head: Mussolini Defiant on South Tyrol
1926-02-06.body: Signor Mussolini has made a defiant speech upholding the Italianization of South Tyrol and warning Germany against interference.

1926-02-06.head: Pancho Villa's Grave Robbed
1926-02-06.body: Unknown persons have broken into the grave of the Mexican revolutionary Pancho Villa at Parral and carried off his skull.

1926-02-07.head: Italian Troops Occupy Jaghbub Oasis
1926-02-07.body: Italian troops have occupied Jaghbub, the desert oasis and Senussi centre transferred to Italian Libya by Egypt under the frontier treaty of December last.

1926-02-07.head: Negro History Week Inaugurated in America
1926-02-07.body: Dr Carter G. Woodson has inaugurated a Negro History Week in the United States.

1926-02-08.head: Berlin Decides to Seek League Membership
1926-02-08.body: The German cabinet has decided unanimously to apply for Germany's admission to the League of Nations.

1926-02-08.head: Geneticist William Bateson Dies
1926-02-08.body: Professor William Bateson, the English biologist who championed Mendel's laws of heredity, has died aged 64.

1926-02-08.head: O'Casey Play Opens at the Abbey
1926-02-08.body: Sean O'Casey's new play The Plough and the Stars has opened at the Abbey Theatre, Dublin.

1926-02-09.head: Stresemann Answers Mussolini in Reichstag
1926-02-09.body: Herr Stresemann has told the Reichstag that Germany rejects Signor Mussolini's statements on South Tyrol.

1926-02-09.head: London Suburbs Under Water
1926-02-09.body: After many days of rain the River Lea has overflowed, flooding suburbs of London.

1926-02-09.head: Plus Ultra Reaches Montevideo
1926-02-09.body: The Spanish flying boat has flown 1,277 miles from Rio de Janeiro to Montevideo.

1926-02-10.head: Germany Applies to Join League of Nations
1926-02-10.body: Germany has formally applied for admission to the League of Nations. A special session of the Assembly is to be called.

1926-02-10.head: Spanish Airmen Reach Buenos Aires
1926-02-10.body: Major Ramon Franco and the Plus Ultra have reached Buenos Aires, completing the 6,300-mile flight from Spain in under 51 hours' flying time.

1926-02-11.head: Mexico Nationalises Church Property
1926-02-11.body: The Calles government has ordered the nationalisation of all Roman Catholic Church property in Mexico.

1926-02-11.head: Riot at Abbey Theatre Performance
1926-02-11.body: The Dublin performance of O'Casey's The Plough and the Stars was disrupted by protesters in the audience.

1926-02-12.head: American Anthracite Strike Ends After 165 Days
1926-02-12.body: The anthracite coal strike in Pennsylvania, the longest in American history, has been settled with the signing of a new contract.

1926-02-12.head: Irish Committee on Evil Literature Named
1926-02-12.body: Mr Kevin O'Higgins, Free State Minister for Justice, has appointed a Committee on Evil Literature.

1926-02-13.head: Mexico Orders Catholic Schools Closed
1926-02-13.body: The Calles government has ordered the closing of Catholic schools throughout Mexico.

1926-02-13.head: Economist F. Y. Edgeworth Dies
1926-02-13.body: Professor Francis Ysidro Edgeworth, the Oxford political economist, has died aged 80.

1926-02-14.head: Bushfires Kill 31 in Victoria
1926-02-14.body: Bushfires have swept the forests near Warburton and Powelltown, Victoria, Australia, killing 31 people.

1926-02-14.head: Abadia Mendez Elected President of Colombia
1926-02-14.body: Dr Miguel Abadia Mendez has been elected President of Colombia, virtually without opposition.

1926-02-15.head: Mackenzie King Wins By-Election
1926-02-15.body: Canadian Prime Minister Mackenzie King has won the Prince Albert by-election in Saskatchewan and regains a seat in the Commons.

1926-02-15.head: Jia Deyao Acting Premier of China
1926-02-15.body: Jia Deyao has been installed as acting Premier of the Peking government.

1926-02-16.head: Soviet Russia Recognises Ibn Saud
1926-02-16.body: The Soviet Union has recognised Abdul Aziz ibn Saud as King of the Hejaz and Sultan of Nejd, the first power to do so.

1926-02-16.head: Mlle Lenglen Beats Miss Wills at Cannes
1926-02-16.body: Suzanne Lenglen of France defeated Helen Wills of America in the much-heralded tennis match at Cannes.

1926-02-17.head: Turkish Assembly Adopts New Civil Code
1926-02-17.body: The Grand National Assembly at Angora has approved a new Civil Code on the Swiss model, replacing religious law in civil matters.

1926-02-17.head: Avalanche Buries Utah Mining Camp
1926-02-17.body: An avalanche has struck the mining camp of Highland Boy in Bingham Canyon, Utah, killing dozens of miners and residents.

1926-02-17.head: Steamer Sinks in Port of Spain
1926-02-17.body: The Trinidad steamer Naparima sank after a collision in Port of Spain harbour. Eleven persons were drowned.

1926-02-18.head: Commons Debates the Iraq Treaty
1926-02-18.body: The House of Commons has debated the new Anglo-Iraq Treaty signed at Baghdad last month.

1926-02-18.head: Citroen Opens Factory at Slough
1926-02-18.body: The French motor firm Citroen has opened a factory at Slough, the largest in Britain under one roof.

1926-02-19.head: Iraq Treaty Discussion Continues in London
1926-02-19.body: The Commons debate on the Anglo-Iraq Treaty, extending British obligations in Iraq for 25 years, continues to draw comment in London.
1926-02-19.note: No major event dated 19 Feb on source page; follow-up to Commons debate of 18 Feb.

1926-02-20.head: Berlin Opens Green Week Farm Fair
1926-02-20.body: The first International Green Week, an exhibition of food and agriculture, has opened in Berlin.

1926-02-21.head: Physicist Kamerlingh Onnes Dies
1926-02-21.body: Professor Heike Kamerlingh Onnes of Leyden, Nobel laureate who first liquefied helium, has died aged 72.

1926-02-21.head: Great Republican Rally in Hamburg
1926-02-21.body: The Reichsbanner Black-Red-Gold, the German republican defence league, has held a mass rally in Hamburg.

1926-02-22.head: Germany Awaits Special League Assembly
1926-02-22.body: Germany's application for League membership now awaits a special Assembly at Geneva in March, amid rival claims by other powers to Council seats.
1926-02-22.note: No event dated 22 Feb on source page; ongoing story following German application of 10 Feb.

1926-02-23.head: Coolidge Opposes Large Air Force
1926-02-23.body: President Coolidge has declared against Colonel Mitchell's call for a large air force, calling such a policy militaristic.

1926-02-24.head: Airman Killed Flying Under Eiffel Tower
1926-02-24.body: French pilot Leon Collet was killed attempting to fly his aeroplane beneath the arch of the Eiffel Tower.

1926-02-25.head: King Prajadhipok Crowned in Bangkok
1926-02-25.body: Prajadhipok has been crowned King Rama VII of Siam in the Grand Palace at Bangkok.

1926-02-26.head: Coolidge Signs Tax Reduction Act
1926-02-26.body: President Coolidge has signed the Revenue Act of 1926, reducing American income and inheritance taxes.

1926-02-26.head: Tiger Flowers Wins Middleweight Title
1926-02-26.body: Tiger Flowers defeated Harry Greb at Madison Square Garden to become world middleweight boxing champion, the first Negro to hold the title.

1926-02-27.head: Maharaja of Indore Abdicates
1926-02-27.body: Tukoji Rao Holkar III has abdicated as Maharaja of Indore after a 23-year reign and is succeeded by his son.
1926-02-27.note: Abdication listed on the February page without a secure day; placed on the nearest thin day.

1926-02-28.head: Astronomer Alphonse Borrelly Dies
1926-02-28.body: Alphonse Borrelly of the Marseilles Observatory, discoverer of several comets, has died aged 83.

1926-03-01.head: RAF Machines Leave Cairo for the Cape
1926-03-01.body: Four Royal Air Force Fairey machines have left Cairo on a long-distance flight to Cape Town and back to England.

1926-03-01.head: Turkey Adopts New Penal Code
1926-03-01.body: Turkey has adopted a new criminal code modelled on that of Italy.

1926-03-01.head: Washington Luis Elected President of Brazil
1926-03-01.body: Dr Washington Luis, Governor of Sao Paulo, has been elected President of Brazil with almost all votes cast.

1926-03-02.head: Wristwatch for Statue of Liberty Refused
1926-03-02.body: The American War Department has declined a New York watchmaker's offer to fit an illuminated wristwatch to the Statue of Liberty.

1926-03-03.head: Shakespeare Biographer Sir Sidney Lee Dies
1926-03-03.body: Sir Sidney Lee, biographer of Shakespeare and Queen Victoria and editor of the Dictionary of National Biography, has died aged 66.

1926-03-04.head: Zizi Lambrino Sues Prince Carol
1926-03-04.body: Mme Zizi Lambrino, first wife of Prince Carol of Romania, has filed suit in Paris against him for ten million francs.

1926-03-05.head: Rutenberg Wins Palestine Power Concession
1926-03-05.body: The High Commissioner has granted Mr Pinhas Rutenberg an exclusive 70-year concession to generate electricity from the waters of the Jordan and Yarmuk.

1926-03-05.head: Aviation Pioneer Clement Ader Dies
1926-03-05.body: Clement Ader, the French engineer who built flying machines in the 1890s, has died aged 84.

1926-03-06.head: Briand Government Falls in France
1926-03-06.body: The Briand ministry has fallen after defeat on its finance bill in the Chamber by 274 votes to 221.

1926-03-06.head: Fire Destroys Shakespeare Memorial Theatre
1926-03-06.body: The Shakespeare Memorial Theatre at Stratford-upon-Avon has been destroyed by fire.

1926-03-07.head: Wireless Telephone Call Crosses the Atlantic
1926-03-07.body: The first two-way wireless telephone conversation between New York and London has been held, marking the telephone's fiftieth anniversary.

1926-03-08.head: League Assembly Meets on German Entry
1926-03-08.body: A special Assembly of the League of Nations has opened at Geneva to consider Germany's admission.

1926-03-09.head: Briand Forms New French Cabinet
1926-03-09.body: M. Aristide Briand has formed his ninth ministry, replacing six ministers and retaining the Foreign Office himself.

1926-03-09.head: Seattle Elects Woman Mayor
1926-03-09.body: Mrs Bertha Knight Landes has been elected Mayor of Seattle, the first woman to head a large American city.

1926-03-10.head: Council Seat Dispute Stalls Geneva
1926-03-10.body: The League Assembly at Geneva remains deadlocked over demands by Poland, Brazil and Spain for Council seats alongside Germany.
1926-03-10.note: No event dated 10 Mar on source page; ongoing League session story (opened 8 Mar).

1926-03-11.head: De Valera Resigns Sinn Fein Presidency
1926-03-11.body: Mr Eamon de Valera has resigned as President of Sinn Fein at the party's Ard-Fheis in Dublin.

1926-03-12.head: Japanese Warship Bombards Taku Forts
1926-03-12.body: A Japanese warship has shelled the Taku Forts near Tientsin, killing several Kuominchun soldiers guarding them.

1926-03-13.head: Cobham Completes Cape to London Flight
1926-03-13.body: Mr Alan Cobham has landed in England from Cape Town, completing the first return air voyage between London and South Africa by way of Cairo.

1926-03-14.head: Costa Rica Train Plunges Into Ravine
1926-03-14.body: A pilgrim train has fallen from the bridge over the Virilla River in Costa Rica, with heavy loss of life.

1926-03-15.head: Brazil Threatens League Deadlock
1926-03-15.body: At Geneva, Brazil's demand for a permanent Council seat continues to block agreement on Germany's admission to the League.
1926-03-15.note: No event dated 15 Mar on source page; ongoing League session story.

1926-03-16.head: Powers Send Ultimatum to Peking
1926-03-16.body: Envoys of the Boxer Protocol powers have demanded that the Peking government remove the defences and blockade at the Taku Forts.

1926-03-16.head: Matteotti Murder Trial Opens at Chieti
1926-03-16.body: Five Fascists accused of the 1924 murder of the Socialist deputy Giacomo Matteotti have gone on trial at Chieti.

1926-03-16.head: Segrave Sets Motor Speed Record
1926-03-16.body: Major Henry Segrave drove a Sunbeam at 152.33 miles an hour on the sands near Southport, a new world record.

1926-03-17.head: League Fails to Admit Germany
1926-03-17.body: The special League Assembly has adjourned without admitting Germany, after Brazil blocked the Council arrangements.

1926-03-17.head: General Brusilov Dies in Moscow
1926-03-17.body: General Alexei Brusilov, commander of the great Russian offensive of 1916, has died aged 72.

1926-03-17.head: Czechoslovak Cabinet Resigns
1926-03-17.body: M. Svehla, Prime Minister of Czechoslovakia, has resigned with his cabinet. M. Jan Cerny has been asked to form a new government.

1926-03-18.head: Troops Fire on Peking Demonstrators
1926-03-18.body: Government troops and police have fired on students protesting against the foreign ultimatum in Peking, killing 47 and wounding some 200.

1926-03-18.head: Academy of Athens Established
1926-03-18.body: An Academy of Athens has been established as Greece's highest institution of learning and research.

1926-03-19.head: Heidelberg Astronomer Finds New Minor Planet
1926-03-19.body: Professor Max Wolf of Heidelberg has discovered a new asteroid.

1926-03-19.head: New York Police Seize Whittemore Gang
1926-03-19.body: New York police have arrested seven members of the Whittemore gang, wanted for jewel robberies.

1926-03-20.head: Chiang Kai-shek Moves Against Canton Communists
1926-03-20.body: General Chiang Kai-shek has proclaimed martial law in Canton and arrested Communist officers after an incident aboard the gunboat Chungshan.

1926-03-20.head: Queen Mother Louise of Denmark Dies
1926-03-20.body: Queen Louise, widow of King Frederick VIII of Denmark and mother of King Christian X and King Haakon of Norway, has died aged 74.

1926-03-21.head: Peking Mourns Massacre Victims
1926-03-21.body: Indignation continues in Peking over Thursday's shooting of student demonstrators, with the Tuan Chi-jui government under heavy criticism.
1926-03-21.note: No event dated 21 Mar on source page; ongoing story from 18 Mar.

1926-03-22.head: Brazilian Steamer Burns on the Amazon
1926-03-22.body: The Brazilian passenger ship Paes de Carvalho has caught fire and sunk in the Amazon River.

1926-03-23.head: De Valera Organises New Republican Party
1926-03-23.body: Mr de Valera has begun organising a new political party in the Irish Free State following his break with Sinn Fein.

1926-03-24.head: Verdict in Matteotti Murder Trial
1926-03-24.body: The Chieti court has acquitted two Fascists and sentenced three to reduced terms for the Matteotti killing, largely cancelled by amnesty.

1926-03-24.head: Cierva Autogiro Company Formed
1926-03-24.body: A company has been formed in England to develop Senor de la Cierva's autogiro flying machine.

1926-03-25.head: French Franc Falls to Record Low
1926-03-25.body: The French franc continues to slide on the exchanges amid the government's financial difficulties, touching the lowest levels in its history against the dollar.
1926-03-25.note: Franc's March 1926 record low is on the March page without a secure day; ongoing story.

1926-03-26.head: Egyptologist Georges Benedite Dies
1926-03-26.body: M. Georges Benedite, curator of Egyptian antiquities at the Louvre, has died aged 68.

1926-03-26.head: Kalman's Circus Princess Opens in Vienna
1926-03-26.body: Emmerich Kalman's new operetta Die Zirkusprinzessin has been given its first performance at the Theater an der Wien.

1926-03-27.head: Bratianu Resigns in Romania
1926-03-27.body: M. Ion Bratianu has resigned as Prime Minister of Romania.

1926-03-27.head: Cambridge Win the Boat Race
1926-03-27.body: Cambridge defeated Oxford by five lengths in the annual University Boat Race on the Thames.

1926-03-27.head: Weill Opera Premiered in Dresden
1926-03-27.body: Kurt Weill's one-act opera Der Protagonist, to a libretto by Georg Kaiser, has been given its first performance at the Dresden State Opera.

1926-03-28.head: Franz Ferdinand's 1914 Manifesto Published
1926-03-28.body: The accession manifesto prepared by the late Archduke Franz Ferdinand before his assassination in 1914 has been published.

1926-03-29.head: American Brewers Permitted Malt Tonic
1926-03-29.body: The United States government has permitted breweries to make a 3.76 per cent alcohol malt tonic, to be sold as medicine.

1926-03-30.head: Averescu Again Prime Minister of Romania
1926-03-30.body: General Alexandru Averescu has become Prime Minister of Romania for the third time, succeeding M. Bratianu.

1926-03-30.head: Farinacci Resigns Fascist Party Post
1926-03-30.body: Signor Roberto Farinacci has resigned as General Secretary of the Fascist Party. Signor Augusto Turati has been chosen to succeed him.

1926-03-30.head: France Ships Convicts to Devil's Island
1926-03-30.body: The French government has shipped 340 convicts to the penal settlement at Devil's Island, Guiana.

1926-03-31.head: Averescu Cabinet Takes Office in Bucharest
1926-03-31.body: General Averescu's new Romanian ministry has taken up its duties following M. Bratianu's resignation.
1926-03-31.note: No event dated 31 Mar on source page; follow-up to the Romanian change of government of 27-30 Mar.
